page: Microsoft Azure D16_v3 is a Dv3-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports hardware-assisted virtualization, AES cryptography, and AVX vector extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

The server is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes 410 GB of local storage but does not feature a dedicated GPU. Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split. Single-core performance is low, with stress-ng single-core, geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests, fall into the average tier, representing the middle 50% of tested hardware.

Memory performance shows average read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks, but large-block write bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. This indicates a potential bottleneck for write-heavy memory operations. For database workloads, the instance achieves average performance in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations, processing 9.27 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput and software compilation also register in the average tier. Given these characteristics, the D16_v3 is appropriate for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and moderate database operations that leverage its 16 vCPUs rather than single-threaded tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D16_v3 is a Dv3-family virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 physical cores, a 2.3 GHz clock speed, and 410 GB of local storage. Benchmark data reveals a performance tradeoff: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression tasks score in the bottom 10%, while multi-core operations, software compilation, and PassMark CPU tests perform in the average tier. Memory read bandwidth is average, but large-block write bandwidth is weak. With average performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving, this server is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose applications, moderate database workloads, and web serving that can utilize its balanced resource allocation without requiring high single-core performance.
